proposal.description: On a host read, capture wins over clear: fault_reg is loaded with the causes live on that clock instead of being emptied
proposal.reason: A read landing while a cause is live and the converter is running leaves fault_reg non-empty on the next clock instead of zero, and because fault_reg never passes through empty, fault_time stays at 0 instead of re-latching the new episode's start time.

proposal.description: fault_time capture takes priority over its clear-on-read, the opposite of fault_reg
proposal.reason: When a host read lands on the clock a first cause appears in an empty fault_reg, fault_time takes timestamp_ms while fault_reg stays empty; if the cause was gone by the next clock, fault_time is left non-zero beside an empty fault_reg.

proposal.description: Episode start is detected from fault_reg having gone non-empty rather than from the capture conditions, so fault_time is latched one clock after the first cause
proposal.reason: fault_time is still 0 on the clock fault_reg first shows a cause and takes the timestamp one clock later, which is the next millisecond's value when the first cause arrives on the clock before timestamp_ms increments.

proposal.description: The episode is judged empty by fault_time being zero instead of fault_reg being zero
proposal.reason: An episode that begins while timestamp_ms is 0 (the first millisecond after reset, or after the counter wraps) does not hold its start time: fault_time is overwritten with the later timestamp while any cause is still live after the counter moves on.

proposal.description: OVP is inferred against the recorded LATCH bit instead of the live latch_assert
proposal.reason: A CPLD-originated trip with latch_assert and latch_state both high and LATCH not yet recorded (the first clock, or after a host read) falsely sets the OVP bit, and a real analog OVP trip after an unread earlier CPLD trip is not recorded.

proposal.description: Over-temperature bypasses the capture gate: with otp_state high, causes are recorded even while the converter is stopped
proposal.reason: With ss_active and run_active both low, otp_state high sets the OTP bit (and any other live cause's bit, such as UVLO during power-down) in fault_reg where it should stay empty, with fault_time left at 0.

proposal.description: UVLO is recorded only in S_RUN; a UVLO that interrupts soft start is forgotten
proposal.reason: With ss_active high and uvlo_state asserted, the UVLO bit of fault_reg stays 0 while fault_time still latches a timestamp for an episode with no cause in it.

proposal.description: The clear-on-read leaves the OVP bit set; only the four lower cause bits are cleared
proposal.reason: After an inferred OVP has been recorded, a host read leaves fault_reg at 5'b10000 instead of 0, so every later read reports OVP until reset and later episodes never see an empty register to latch a new fault_time.

after: fault_reg <= fault_reg & {ovp, latch_assert, otp_state, uvlo_state, (window_trip || window_trip_SS)};
proposal.description: A host read clears only the recorded causes that have gone away; a recorded cause still asserted survives the read, even with the converter stopped
proposal.reason: With the converter stopped after a fault and the condition still present (UVLO still low, OTP still hot), a read leaves that bit set in fault_reg where the original returns to 0 and stays there because capture is gated off.

proposal.description: Causes are captured through a priority chain, one per clock, instead of independently accumulated
proposal.reason: When two causes are live together while the converter is running (for example otp_state with uvlo_state, or window_trip with latch_assert), only the first in the chain is recorded and the other bit of fault_reg stays 0 for as long as the first remains asserted.

proposal.description: The OVERCURRENT bit follows the live window trips while running instead of being set and held
proposal.reason: If the window trip deasserts while ss_active or run_active is still high, bit 0 of fault_reg drops back to 0 before the host has read it, so a transient overcurrent is no longer reported.

proposal.description: A host read clears fault_reg only when the converter is stopped; a read during S_SS or S_RUN does not clear it
proposal.reason: Reading the register while ss_active or run_active is high leaves the earlier causes in fault_reg although the cause conditions are gone, while fault_time is cleared to 0, so the record keeps stale bits with no start time.

proposal.description: latch_assert also sets the OVERCURRENT bit, on the assumption that every CPLD latch trip is an overcurrent
proposal.reason: With latch_assert high and neither window trip asserted while the converter is running, fault_reg reads 5'b01001 instead of 5'b01000.
